$comment: DRAFT — not a shipped contract. Authority: docs/01-CONTRACT.md §12 (which DECLINES to define a projection at all, on Workbench rule 8) and docs/10-V11-SCOPE.md §4 (the four laws this artifact is built to satisfy instead). Written from crates/engine-core/src/html.rs. A PROJECTION, not the record: the representation is the evidence, this is derived from it and is deliberately lossy, and `coverage` is where it says how. SECOND projection, deliberately not a rendering of the first — see `html_rule`.
title: ethos.html.v1
description: An HTML projection of a DocumentRepresentation, carried TOGETHER WITH the Anchor Map that inverts it back to representation nodes, a coverage census of every source character that did not reach it, and a second census of the structure the projection could not carry (v1.1-S4). It obeys the same four laws as `ethos.markdown.v1` and exists for one reason that artifact cannot serve: GFM has no `rowspan`, so the Markdown projection must expand a merged cell and count the slots that costs, while `<td rowspan>` carries the merge the document actually drew. The consumer's rule is one line: a quote that touches a `syntax` byte is not invertible.

parser_version.description: The engine build that produced this artifact.

profile_sha256.description: Hash of the pinned configuration profile. Two artifacts are comparable if and only if this matches — and since v1.1-S4 the profile carries `html_rule` beside `markdown_rule`, so a run under a different projection rule is correctly non-comparable.

source_sha256.description: Digest of the original source bytes, carried through from the representation.

representation_sha256.description: Digest of the representation this projects. The binding that makes the map checkable: without it, a map could name node ids from a different parse of a different file and read exactly the same.

html_rule.description:
Version id of the projection rule. `html-blocks-v2` (v1.1-S4) emits `

`, `

`-`

` from the structure tree only, `
    `/`
  • ` from a tagged `/L`, and `` with the document's merges carried as `rowspan`/`colspan`. Every cell is a `
    `: neither detector reads `/TH`, so a header row would be invented. SEPARATE from `markdown_rule` and it moves independently — a change to how a `` is spelled is not a change to how a GFM row is. Source bytes are ENTITY-ENCODED: `&`, `<` and `>` come out as `&`, `<`, `>`, the whole entity sits inside the `source` segment because `<` contains no `<` to label, and inverting a source segment therefore means HTML-unescaping it — a total, lossless transform. The census counts the CHARACTERS the document drew, not the bytes the entity took.

html.description: The HTML, as a FRAGMENT: no `<html>`, `<head>`, `<body>` or doctype, because those are bytes no document drew and the consumer's framing is theirs to choose. NEVER emitted without `anchor_map`: they are fields of one artifact rather than two files, because a companion file is a thing a pipeline strips and a field is not.

anchor_map.description: The map from `html` bytes back to evidence. Its segments TOTAL-TILE the string: sorted, contiguous, no overlap, no gap, covering 0..len(html) exactly. A map with a hole is worse than no map, because the hole is exactly where an unquotable byte hides — so an incomplete map is a hard error on both construction and parse, never a warning.

kind.description: TWO values, deliberately. `source` inverts to canonical node text; `syntax` is markup the exporter invented. There is no third — a 'probably source' would be the confidence field docs/01-CONTRACT.md §9 forbids, and would put the consumer back to guessing whether a quote is citable.

start.description: First UTF-8 BYTE offset into `html`, inclusive. Bytes rather than characters, and the description says so: every language's slice takes one or the other, and saying which is the difference between a map and a hint.

node_ids.description: The representation nodes these bytes came from, in emission order. Present on `source` and ABSENT on `syntax`, because syntax came from no node. Never a newly minted id: a projection that invented identifiers would be a second record of one document, and two records drift.

coverage.description: A census, not a summary. `source_chars_emitted + source_chars_dropped == source_chars_in_representation`, asserted in CI on real fixtures. Counted in CHARACTERS of node text, because the thing being conserved is the text the representation offered.

source_chars_in_representation.description: Sum of the character count of every node's text in the representation — the RAW text, not its normalization, so that whitespace the projection collapsed is visible as a bucket rather than hidden by moving the denominator.

source_chars_emitted.description: Characters that landed in a `source` segment.

source_chars_dropped.description: Characters that did not, summed over `dropped`.

dropped.description: Where the dropped characters went, by named class, sorted by code. Checklist A14: if something is removed, the artifact says so AND says how much. 'Some content was omitted' is not a disclosure; `annotation-text-not-projected-v1: 37` is.

structural_erasures.description: Structure the projection flattened, by named class, sorted by code. On this artifact it is almost always EMPTY, and that is the point of having two projections: the `gfm-*` codes name things GFM cannot say, and HTML says them. The one exception is `gfm-list-item-run-joins-v1` — two sibling `/LI`s have identical role paths, so nothing in the representation distinguishes 'the rest of this item' from 'the next item' and BOTH projections must guess. Its `gfm-` prefix is historical: the erasure belongs to the tagged tree, and it carries the name of the slice that first met it.

code.description: `gfm-span-slots-unrepresentable-v1` — slots a merged cell covered that GFM cannot say it covered, `rowspan × colspan - 1` summed over the table's cells. `gfm-row-zero-separator-v1` — once per GFM table, because the delimiter row makes row 0 a header on every renderer and neither detector reads `/TH`. `gfm-cell-run-claimed-twice-v1` — a run two cells both claimed, emitted under the first so that one node's characters are not counted twice. `gfm-cell-not-placed-v1` — a cell outside the declared grid or on a taken slot; its runs still project, as paragraphs. `gfm-table-not-projected-v1` — a table with zero rows or columns. `gfm-list-item-run-joins-v1` — a body run appended to an already-open list item, which is the one boundary a role path cannot settle.

count.description: How many. Never a severity and never a ratio (docs/01-CONTRACT.md §9). Only non-zero classes appear: a list of codes all reading `0` is the disclosure-shaped noise a reader learns to skip, and every code is documented here whether or not a document trips it.
